question: On Bank of America's second-quarter 2026 earnings call (July 14, 2026), what full-year 2026 outlook did the CFO give for (a) net interest income (NII) growth and (b) operating leverage, and how did each compare with the outlook he said had been given earlier in 2026 (in January and/or April)?
grading: Key points (all required): (1) full-year 2026 NII growth expected at the UPPER END of the 6%-8% range (not a new numeric range); (2) full-year 2026 operating leverage expected in the range of 300 to 400 basis points; (3) comparison with earlier outlook: NII growth was 5%-7% in January and raised to 6%-8% in April; operating leverage was 'more than 200 basis points' as of the April (Q1) call. Accept equivalent wording ('top end of 6-8%', '3-4 percentage points'). Fail if the answer gives plain 6%-8% or 5%-7% as the current NII view without 'upper end', gives 'more than 200 bps' as the current operating-leverage view, states a dollar NII figure as guidance, or relies on remarks from the Q3 2026 call (mid-October 2026, after the as_of date) or the mid-September Barclays conference.
answer: (a) Full-year 2026 NII growth is now expected at the upper end of the 6%-8% range (the CFO recalled 5%-7% in January, raised to 6%-8% in April) [W01-E1]. (b) Full-year 2026 operating leverage is now expected to be 300 to 400 basis points, up from 'more than 200 basis points' given on the April call; first-half 2026 operating leverage had already exceeded 450 bps (Q2: 6.6%) [W01-E1]. Neither full-year outlook appears in the July 14 press release or in the slide deck filed with the 8-K [W01-E2, W01-E3].

output.answer:
On Bank of America’s Q2 2026 earnings call on July 14, 2026, CFO Alastair Borthwick raised the company’s full‑year 2026 guidance for both metrics versus the outlooks given earlier in the year.

| Metric | July 14, 2026 Outlook | Prior 2026 Outlook(s) | Comparison |
|--------|----------------------|-----------------------|------------|
| **(a) Net Interest Income (NII) growth** | Upper end of the **6%–8%** range (effectively ~8%) | **January:** **5%–7%**; **April (Q1):** raised to **6%–8%** | Raised twice during 2026; the July guidance landed at the top of the April range[^6^][^1^] |
| **(b) Operating leverage** | **300–400 bps** | **April (Q1):** **“more than 200 bps”** (alternatively framed as the medium‑term **200–300 bps** target) | Raised by 100 bps at the low end, lifting the floor from ~200 bps to 300 bps after a strong first half (450 bps through June)[^5^][^2^][^9^] |

**Key details from the call**

* **NII:** Borthwick explicitly reminded analysts: *“In January, we told you to expect 5%–7% full year NII growth. In April, we raised that full year range to be 6%–8%”* and said the bank now expected to finish at the **upper end of that 6%–8% range**, assuming modest loan/deposit growth and one 25 bp rate hike in September[^6^][^1^].

* **Operating leverage:** After delivering **660 bps** of operating leverage in Q2 and **~450 bps** in the first half, Borthwick lifted the full‑year target. He noted that the bank had previously committed to a **200–300 bp** medium‑term framework, but the strong H1 performance gave confidence to guide **above that range**, settling on **300–400 bps** for the full year[^5^][^2^].

**Sources**

* Motley Fool Q2 2026 transcript (July 14, 2026): https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/21/bank-of-america-bac-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript
* Alpha Sense Q2 2026 summary: https://www.alpha-sense.com/earnings/bac
* Hudson Labs Q3 2026 preview (summarizing Q2 guidance changes): https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/bank-of-america-q3-2026-earnings-preview-bac-results-preview
* BigGo Finance Q1 2026 recap (April 15, 2026, showing earlier NII and operating leverage guidance): https://finance.biggo.com/news/US_BAC_2026-04-15
